candidates.title: Pegvisomant in severe, treatment-resistant thyroid eye disease: a case report.
candidates.abstract: Teprotumumab, a monoclonal antibody against the IGF1 receptor, has proven effective in the treatment of thyroid eye disease (TED). Pegvisomant reduces IGF1 levels through selective inhibition of growth hormone receptors. Here, we present a hypothesis-generating case of a 69-year-old patient with progressive TED. Pegvisomant 20 mg was administered daily for 90 days. IGF1 levels declined and remained low-normal during treatment. Clinical activity scores and VISA (vision, inflammation, strabismus and appearance) scores improved rapidly. MRI assessment showed that water content of both extraocular muscles and orbital connective tissue decreased after treatment. 99mTc-DTPA SPECT confirmed the decrease in disease activity. Further studies may confirm the efficacy of pegvisomant in TED. A 69-year-old female patient with severe, active thyroid eye disease (TED) – a condition linked to Graves’ disease where the body’s immune system attacks tissues around the eyes – presented with bulging eyes (proptosis), double vision, eye redness, swelling and reduced visual sharpness.Prior treatments with standard therapies for TED, including intravenous steroid courses, radiation therapy targeting the orbit (eye socket) and the biological drug rituximab, failed to achieve improvement. TED progresses in part because proteins called IGF1 receptors on the surface of eye-socket tissues are overactivated. The researchers hypothesized that using pegvisomant, which is a medication typically used for acromegaly (hormone imbalance) that lowers insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF1) levels in the blood, would reduce activation of these receptors and ease eye inflammation.The patient received a daily 20 mg injection of pegvisomant for 90 days. Symptom improvement The patient experienced a rapid reduction in eye pain, redness and swelling, alongside marked improvement in visual sharpness and colour vision within 8 weeks.MRI and imaging results Orbital MRI and nuclear imaging showed a distinct drop in tissue inflammation and fluid accumulation (oedema) in the muscles around the eye.Proptosis and double vision Eye bulging and double vision did not significantly change during the trial.Safety Pegvisomant was well tolerated with no reported side effects, and her blood sugar and liver function remained stable. Blood IGF1 levels dropped as expected and returned to normal after treatment ended. Pegvisomant rapidly reduced eye inflammation and improved vision in a patient whose TED had resisted standard therapies. However, because this was a single case study, the delayed effects from previous treatments cannot be entirely ruled out. Further clinical trials are needed to determine if pegvisomant is effective at higher doses or when given earlier in the disease course.

candidates.title: Endocrine therapies and hormonal dysfunction after traumatic brain injury: A scoping review.
candidates.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with current management strategies primarily focused on preventing secondary injury rather than modifying disease progression. Post-traumatic endocrine dysfunction has emerged as a significant and potentially treatable contributor to outcomes after TBI. A scoping review was conducted following PRISMA-ScR guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to September 2025 for clinical studies evaluating endocrine dysfunction and endocrine-targeted therapies post-TBI. Eligible studies included clinical trials and observational studies reporting either an endocrine outcome following TBI or an endocrine-targeted intervention with clinical or biochemical outcomes. Sixty-seven studies met the inclusion criteria. Endocrine dysfunction was common, affecting multiple hormone axes, with growth hormone (GH) deficiency being the most frequently reported deficiency; hypoprolactinemia and hyperprolactinemia were also identified and are increasingly recognized contributors to post-TBI metabolic morbidity. Growth hormone replacement therapy demonstrated improvements in cognitive function, fatigue, mood, and quality of life in several studies; however, its effects on functional outcomes and mortality were inconsistent. Progesterone showed benefit in early-phase trials but failed to demonstrate efficacy in large multicenter randomized controlled trials, an inconsistency that appears closely tied to the timing of treatment initiation after injury. Other therapies, including desmopressin and glucocorticoids, were primarily used for supportive management, with limited evidence of neuroprotective benefit. Endocrine dysfunction after TBI is prevalent, heterogeneous, and associated with worse clinical outcomes. While endocrine therapies, particularly GH, show promise, their translation into clinical practice is limited by heterogeneity in study design, small sample sizes, and inconsistent findings. Larger, well-designed trials and consensus clinical guidelines are needed to define optimal therapeutic strategies and integrate endocrine care into the optimal management of TBI patients.
candidates.journal: Growth hormone & IGF research : official journal of the Growth Hormone Research Society and the International IGF Research Society

candidates.title: Diagnostic challenges of masked arginine vasopressin deficiency in neurosarcoidosis complicated by sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor use.
candidates.abstract: A wide variety of endocrine disorders caused by sarcoidosis have been reported to date. We report the case of an 82-year-old male patient who presented with hypercalcemia and anterior pituitary hormone deficiency at the time of his sarcoidosis diagnosis and was subsequently diagnosed with arginine vasopressin deficiency (AVP-D) 6 months after the initiation of glucocorticoid therapy. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed an enlarged pituitary gland, thickened pituitary stalk, and loss of the posterior pituitary bright spot, raising the suspicion of hypothalamic-pituitary sarcoidosis. Despite improvement in hypercalcemia, anterior pituitary function, and pituitary enlargement and stalk thickening with glucocorticoid therapy, subjective symptoms of dry mouth and polyuria gradually became apparent several months after the start of treatment. While the characteristic hypotonic polyuria of AVP-D was not prominent, we surmised that these typical clinical features were masked by adrenal insufficiency, chronic kidney disease (CKD), and concurrent use of a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor for type 2 diabetes. This case highlights the fact that the typical presentation of AVP-D can be masked by concurrent SGLT2 inhibitor use and CKD, emphasizing careful assessment of water balance in such patients.

candidates.title: A novel multiplex digital PCR assay for simultaneous quantification of androgen receptor amplification, mutations, and splice variants in cell-free nucleic acids from metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.
candidates.abstract: Somatic androgen receptor (AR) alterations including gene amplification, point mutations, and the AR-V7 splice variant occur in 50-70% of patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) and drive resistance to AR-pathway inhibitors (ARPIs) in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). However, current liquid biopsy approaches typically require separate cell-free DNA (cfDNA) and cfRNA workflows to evaluate these distinct alteration classes, increasing sample input requirements, assay complexity, and cost. Because plasma cell-free nucleic acid yield is often limited, an integrated assay capable of interrogating DNA and RNA-derived biomarkers from a single blood draw remain an unmet clinical need. Here we describe the development and proof-of-concept validation of a novel multiplex multimodal digital PCR (dPCR) assay that co-detects AR copy-number amplification, somatic point mutations (T878A), and the AR-V7 splice variant from plasma cell-free nucleic acids (cfNAs) in a single streamlined reaction. The assay employs RNase H-dependent PCR (rhPCR) primers with ultra-short amplicons (≤68 bp) that simultaneously interrogate both cfDNA and cfRNA, enabling multimodal detection without separate DNA and RNA workflows. Using prostate cancer cell lines with defined AR alteration status, the assay detected AR amplification at 2% of tumor DNA, quantified T878A mutations at a mutant allele frequency as low as 0.024%, and AR-V7 splicing variant with a sensitivity of 0.096% tumor cell fraction. In two mCRPC patient plasma samples, the assay tracked dynamic changes of these AR variants during ARPI therapy, revealing distinct patterns of clonal evolution that are consistent with treatment pressure and clinical outcomes. This multimodal dPCR platform provides a cost-effective, highly sensitive liquid biopsy tool for detection of clinically significant AR alterations and represents a foundation for a laboratory-developed test (LDT) to guide personalized therapy in mCRPC.

candidates.title: Pituitary Apoplexy Presenting as a Transient Ischemic Attack: An Endocrine Emergency.
candidates.abstract: Pituitary apoplexy (PA) is an endocrine emergency caused by hemorrhage or infarction of a pituitary adenoma and occurs more frequently in males and patients with macroadenomas. It typically presents acutely with headache, visual disturbances, or impaired consciousness. Focal neurological deficits are uncommon and may be mistaken for a primary cerebrovascular event. Acute secondary adrenal insufficiency is a major contributor to hemodynamic instability and mortality. A 67-year-old man with arterial hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease presented with sudden presyncope, followed by dysarthria and right upper limb weakness. He had a five-month history of headache that had worsened abruptly three days before presentation. On admission, he was febrile (38.5 °C), hypotensive (89/49 mmHg), and tachycardic, with dysarthria, mild right central facial palsy, and grade 4 motor strength in the right upper limb (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score of 3). Computed tomography (CT) angiography revealed an enlarged pituitary gland and 90% calcified stenosis of the left internal carotid artery. The focal neurological deficits resolved completely within approximately 30 minutes of arrival, during fluid resuscitation. However, hypotension persisted despite the administration of 2 L of crystalloid. A 200 mg bolus of hydrocortisone was administered for suspected adrenal insufficiency, resulting in prompt hemodynamic recovery. Baseline cortisol was <1 µg/dL, with an inappropriately low adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) concentration. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) confirmed a pituitary macroadenoma with recent hemorrhage, without evidence of infarction on diffusion-weighted imaging. The episode was interpreted as a hemodynamic transient ischemic attack precipitated by PA-associated acute secondary adrenal insufficiency. Antiplatelet therapy, initiated for a presumed primary cerebrovascular event, was discontinued, and the patient was managed conservatively. Follow-up confirmed persistent panhypopituitarism, including central diabetes insipidus, requiring long-term hormone replacement. PA may mimic a cerebrovascular event through direct vascular compromise or, as in this case, hypotension superimposed on pre-existing carotid artery disease. Empirical hydrocortisone treatment should not be delayed pending laboratory confirmation of adrenal insufficiency. Early MRI is essential to establish the diagnosis and guide management before antithrombotic or endovascular treatment is initiated when a sellar abnormality is identified.

candidates.title: Higher ARNT expression is associated with the sparsely granulated phenotype in somatotroph pituitary adenomas: An immunohistochemical study.
candidates.abstract: Somatotroph pituitary adenomas are a heterogeneous group comprising distinct histopathological subtypes, including the well-defined densely granulated (DG) and sparsely granulated (SG) phenotypes. While the aryl hydrocarbon receptor-interacting protein (AIP) pathway has been implicated in pituitary tumorigenesis, the role of aryl hydrocarbon receptor nuclear translocator (ARNT) in somatotroph tumors remains poorly characterized. We retrospectively analyzed 71 surgically treated somatotroph pituitary adenomas, clinically managed in a tertiary endocrinology center between 2020 and 2025. Immunohistochemical expression of AIP, AHR and ARNT was evaluated and correlated with clinicopathological characteristics, including cytokeratin pattern, hormonal expression and Ki-67 index. Moderate/strong ARNT expression was more frequent in SG than in DG adenomas (60% vs. 17.6%, p = 0.002). Patients with moderate/strong ARNT expression were younger than those with absent/weak expression (median 39 vs. 46 years, p = 0.044). In multivariable analysis, ARNT expression remained associated with the SG phenotype after adjustment for age and sex (adjusted OR 6.84, 95% CI 2.05-22.84; p = 0.002). No significant associations were observed between ARNT expression and Ki-67 index, baseline GH or IGF1 levels, AIP/AHR immunoexpression or the evaluated clinical outcomes, including biochemical control during first-generation somatostatin receptor ligand therapy. Increased ARNT expression is associated with the sparsely granulated phenotype in somatotroph pituitary adenomas, suggesting that ARNT expression may reflect tumor differentiation rather than proliferative activity. However, the present findings do not demonstrate additional prognostic or therapeutic utility beyond granulation pattern. Further molecular and transcriptomic studies are warranted to clarify the biological role of ARNT.

candidates.title: Acinetobacter baumannii Nosocomial Meningitis Secondary to Neurosurgical Intervention: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Nosocomial meningitis is a serious complication of neurosurgical procedures, associated with high morbidity and mortality, as well as significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Among the causative pathogens, Acinetobacter baumannii (A. baumannii) is particularly concerning due to its ability to survive for prolonged periods in the hospital environment, its opportunistic virulence, and, especially, its tendency to develop multidrug resistance to antimicrobial agents. Diagnosis is often difficult in the postoperative setting, particularly when the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is altered as a result of the surgical procedure. Rapid identification of the causative agent and early initiation of appropriate antibiotic therapy are essential to limit complications and improve patient prognosis. We report the case of a 27-year-old patient with a history of surgically treated craniopharyngioma complicated by anterior hypopituitarism. Three weeks after surgery, he was admitted to the ICU with suspected postoperative meningitis due to the onset of behavioral disturbances associated with nasal discharge, without a fever. Brain CT was normal. CSF analysis, obtained by lumbar puncture under strict aseptic conditions, revealed a turbid fluid with leukocytosis of 5,760 cells/mm³, predominantly composed of neutrophils, along with elevated protein levels (5.7 g/L) and low glucose levels (0.05 g/L). Direct examination after Gram staining showed Gram-negative coccobacilli with a marked inflammatory reaction. CSF culture grew a multidrug-resistant (MDR) strain of A. baumannii, which was sensitive only to colistin. The patient received antibiotic therapy with colistin, administered intravenously and intrathecally for 18 days, with initial neurological improvement and sterilization of the CSF by the 15th day of treatment. The subsequent course was unfavorable, marked by the development of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) secondary to ventilator-associated pneumonia caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), complicated by refractory septic shock, which ultimately led to his death after one month of hospitalization in the ICU. This report highlights the severity of nosocomial meningitis caused by MDR A. baumannii and underscores the importance of implementing infection prevention measures in healthcare settings.

candidates.title: Prevalence of Mild Autonomous Cortisol Secretion Among Patients With Adrenal Incidentaloma and Its Association With Metabolic Abnormalities: A Hospital-Based, Analytical, Cross-Sectional Study.
candidates.abstract: Background Mild autonomous cortisol secretion (MACS) is a common hormonal abnormality among patients with adrenal incidentaloma and has been associated with cardiometabolic abnormalities. However, evidence regarding its prevalence and metabolic associations in Pakistani populations remains limited. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of MACS among patients with adrenal incidentaloma and evaluate its association with metabolic abnormalities. Methodology A hospital-based, analytical, cross-sectional study was conducted among 380 adults with adrenal incidentaloma at Jinnah Hospital, Lahore, affiliated with Allama Iqbal Medical College, Pakistan. Participants underwent clinical, anthropometric, biochemical, hormonal, and radiological assessment. MACS was evaluated using the 1-mg overnight dexamethasone suppression test, with assessment of morning adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) and dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate to support ACTH-independent cortisol secretion. Metabolic abnormalities, including obesity, central obesity, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, and metabolic syndrome, were assessed. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to evaluate independent associations after adjustment for relevant demographic, lifestyle, clinical, medication-related, and radiological covariates. Results MACS was identified in 95 (25.0%) participants. Compared with patients without MACS, those with MACS had higher frequencies of obesity, central obesity, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, and metabolic syndrome, as well as a greater burden of multiple metabolic abnormalities. After multivariable adjustment, MACS was independently associated with obesity (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) = 1.85, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.09-3.14; p = 0.022), diabetes mellitus (aOR = 1.68, 95% CI = 1.01-2.80; p = 0.046), metabolic syndrome (aOR = 1.82, 95% CI = 1.11-2.98; p = 0.017), and the presence of ≥2 metabolic abnormalities (aOR = 1.92, 95% CI = 1.17-3.15; p = 0.010). Larger adrenal lesion size was independently associated with MACS (aOR = 1.38 per cm, 95% CI = 1.14-1.67; p = 0.001). Conclusions MACS was present in one-quarter of patients with adrenal incidentaloma and was associated with a greater cardiometabolic burden. These findings highlight the potential importance of assessing cortisol secretion and metabolic risk in patients with adrenal incidentaloma, while prospective multicenter studies are needed to clarify the clinical significance and temporal relationships of these associations.

candidates.title: Incidence and mortality of invasive fungal infections among patients admitted in intensive care units in India: findings from a multicentric registry-based study (2023-25).
candidates.abstract: Invasive fungal infections (IFIs) are challenging to treat in critical care, particularly among patients treated in Intensive care units (ICUs). The existing evidence on IFIs from India remains fragmented. This study characterises IFI incidence, risk factors, resistance pattern, treatment and outcome among patients admitted to ICUs. This multicentre observational study leveraged registry data on IFIs among patients admitted to 63 ICUs in eight Advanced Mycology Diagnostic and Research centres in India between January 2023 and November 2025. Patients with proven and probable IFI according to European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer/Mycoses Study Group Education and Research Consortium (EORTC/MSGERC) 2020 and the modified Aspergillus intensive care unit (AspICU) 2020 criteria were included. IFI incidence to hospital admission, all-cause in-hospital mortality, pathogen distribution and antifungal susceptibility were recorded. Mortality-associated factors were estimated using multivariable logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards analysis. Among 178,417 ICU admissions, 2500 IFI patients were identified with an incidence of 14/1000 admissions (95% CI 13.5-14.6) and all-cause mortality of 53.6% (95% CI 51.7-55.6%). Invasive candidiasis was the most frequently reported (57.1%), followed by invasive aspergillosis (37%), mucormycosis (3.4%), trichosporonosis (1.8%), pneumocystis pneumonia (1.1%), and cryptococcosis (1.2%). Median age of the patients was 45 years (IQR: 26-60), with 61.9% males and 38.1% females. Among candidiasis, Candida tropicalis predominated (35.6%), while Candida auris exhibited high fluconazole resistance (61.7%) and elevated amphotericin B minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) (40.7%). Aspergillus fumigatus (50.8%) and Aspergillus flavus (38.7%) predominated among culture-positive aspergillosis, with generally low MICs. Exploratory multivariable analyses showed that sepsis, chronic liver disease, immunosuppression, corticosteroid exposure, and total parenteral nutrition were associated with higher mortality in invasive candidiasis, whereas mechanical ventilation, corticosteroid exposure, and immunosuppression were associated with higher mortality in invasive aspergillosis. The study findings highlight a high IFI burden and mortality among patients admitted in ICUs of India, with mortality exceeding 50%, underscoring the need for continuous surveillance, rapid diagnostics, infection control and antifungal stewardship. This study was funded by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), Delhi (Grant ID: 157401).
candidates.journal: The Lancet regional health. Southeast Asia

candidates.title: Endocrine dysfunctions in patients with beta thalassemia major: a single-center retrospective study from Basrah.
candidates.abstract: The management of patients with beta thalassemia major (BTH) involves regular blood transfusions which are associated with iron overload. This may result in various endocrine dysfunctions (EDs). This study aimed to assess the obesrved frequency of different EDs in patients with transfusion-dependent BTH. A retrospective study that included 496 patients with BTH who were referred from the Basra Center for hereditary blood diseases to Faiha Specialized Diabetes, Endocrine and Metabolsim Center for endocrine-related complaints and underwent detailed endocrine assessments from Jan 2010 to Dec 2023. The mean presentation age for endocrine evaluation was 13.6 ± 6.5 years with no difference between male and female. The commonest clinical presentations of BTH patients in our center were short stature 65.5%, amenorrhea 16.4, hyperglycemia 13.7%, delayed puberty 13.3, and hypocalcemia 5.2%. The proportion patients with ED was 16.8%. The most frequent EDs were growth hormone deficiency (GHD) 6.0%, diabetes mellitus (DM) 4.9%, hypogonadism 4.5%, hypothyroidism 3.2%. Within those patients, 78.7% had single ED, 16.5% had two EDs and 4.8% had three or more EDs. EDs were observed among patients with BTH. The commonest EDs were GHD, DM, and hypogonadism. We recommend regular and timely surveillance using both clinical and hormonal assessment in patients with BTH.

candidates.title: Sinonasal and Olfactory Quality of Life Following Endonasal Transsphenoidal Surgery for Pituitary Adenoma: A Multicenter Prospective Cohort Triphasic Recovery Analysis in Ethiopia.
candidates.abstract: To characterize the sinonasal and olfactory quality of life (QoL) trajectory. A multicenter prospective cohort study was conducted on 91 patients undergoing TSS at Addis Ababa University teaching hospitals between May 2024 and August 2025. QoL was evaluated using the Sino-Nasal Outcome Test (SNOT-22) questionnaire v4 preoperatively and at 3- and 6-month postoperatively. Analysis revealed a characteristic triphasic recovery pattern: low preoperative baseline, a transient peak in morbidity at 3 months, and an improvement toward baseline by 6 months for most systemic domains. At 3 months, significant score worsening occurred for loss of smell/taste (mean: 1.7, p < 0.001), thick discharge (mean: 1.0, p < 0.001), congestion (mean: 1.0, p < 0.001), postnasal discharge (mean: 0.7, p < 0.001), and runny nose (mean: 0.5, p = 0.003). By 6 months, persistence was confined to loss of smell/taste (p < 0.001), thick discharge (p < 0.001), and congestion (p = 0.005). Exploratory analysis in the nasoseptal flap cohort (n = 3) showed higher scores. Preliminary findings of delayed ear pain/fullness in acromegaly at 6 months hypothesized to reflect a link between growth hormone normalization and altered Eustachian tube function. Poorer sleep with binostril access (p = 0.017) speculatively associated with bilateral synechiae under limited postoperative care. Unlike Western cohorts, protracted recovery may reflect lack of standardized high-volume saline irrigation and scheduled debridement. TSS demonstrates a favorable long-term QoL profile; however, localized sinonasal and olfactory deficits often persist at 6 months.

candidates.title: A Case of MEN 2A Syndrome With Bilateral Recurrent Pheochromocytoma: A Case Report and Literature Review.
candidates.abstract: Pheochromocytoma is a neuroendocrine tumor arising from chromaffin cells and producing catecholamines. Due to the excessive release of catecholamines, these tumors can present with paroxysmal episodes of high blood pressure, headache, diaphoresis, and palpitations. We present the case of a 23-year-old female patient who presented to the clinic with a history of headache, palpitations, and vomiting for two months. She was admitted for further investigations and management. Laboratory studies revealed elevated urinary and plasma catecholamine levels. Further work-up revealed bilateral adrenal masses diagnosed as pheochromocytoma and medullary thyroid cancer. The patient was diagnosed with multiple endocrine neoplasia (MEN) type 2 and underwent bilateral laparoscopic adrenalectomy and total thyroidectomy with central and lateral neck dissection, and during surveillance, she was found to have recurrent pheochromocytoma. We also discuss the diagnosis and management of recurrent pheochromocytoma in MEN syndrome.

candidates.title: From Trauma to Tumour: Incidental Giant Left Adrenal Myelolipoma in Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia.
candidates.abstract: Adrenal myelolipomas are rare, benign tumours composed of mature adipose and haematopoietic tissue. Patients with congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) are predisposed to their development, with chronic adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) hypersecretion secondary to impaired cortisol synthesis thought to be the principal driver of myelolipoma formation in this population. A 49-year-old female with known CAH presented to the emergency department following a stab wound to the abdomen. Computed tomography (CT) incidentally identified a 12 cm encapsulated left adrenal lesion consistent with a giant myelolipoma. Despite reported adherence to hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone replacement therapy, persistently elevated adrenal steroid precursors and plasma renin levels suggested suboptimal glucocorticoid control. Following multidisciplinary team (MDT) review, the patient was offered a left adrenalectomy given the lesion size (>10 cm) and concerns regarding the risk of spontaneous haemorrhage. This case underscores the importance of systematic imaging review beyond the primary indication for scanning, and the value of optimising biochemical monitoring and considering adrenal imaging in selected high-risk CAH patients.

candidates.title: B-Lymphoblastic Leukemia Presenting as Bilateral Ovarian Masses in a 20-Year-Old Woman.
candidates.abstract: Hematologic malignancies involving the ovaries are rare and may mimic ovarian carcinoma. We report a 20-year-old woman who presented with generalized body pain, bilateral ovarian masses, and abdominal adenopathy, initially suspected to have ovarian carcinoma. Despite normal blood counts, a retroperitoneal lymph node biopsy and subsequent bone marrow biopsy confirmed B-lymphoblastic leukemia. Molecular analysis identified multiple pathogenic alterations, including CREBBP, KMT2D, and KRAS mutations, CDKN2A copy number loss, and FLT3 overexpression. The patient developed tumor lysis syndrome and was transferred to a tertiary center, after which she was lost to follow-up. While long-term treatment response could not be evaluated, this case underscores the clinical necessity of including B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma in the differential diagnosis of bilateral ovarian masses in young women, even with normal peripheral blood counts. Early tissue diagnosis through minimally invasive biopsy is essential to avoid unnecessary surgery and to initiate appropriate systemic therapy.

candidates.title: A Clinical Insight into Von Hippel-Lindau Syndrome: Diagnostic Challenges.
candidates.abstract: Von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) syndrome is a rare hereditary disorder characterised by the development of multiple benign and malignant tumours across various organs. Caused by mutations in the VHL tumour suppressor gene, it presents a wide range of clinical manifestations, including retinal haemangioblastomas, central nervous system tumours, renal cell carcinoma, pancreatic lesions, and phaeochromocytomas. This report describes the case of a 35-year-old woman who presented with visual impairment and abdominal masses. Imaging revealed typical VHL manifestations, including bilateral renal lesions and pancreatic involvement. Genetic testing confirmed the diagnosis. The patient underwent staged partial nephrectomies, with histopathology confirming clear cell renal cell carcinoma in both kidneys. This case highlights the importance of recognising the variable clinical and radiological presentations of VHL syndrome. Early diagnosis and multidisciplinary management are essential to reduce morbidity and mortality. Increased awareness and regular surveillance are critical for timely detection and intervention in patients with VHL syndrome.

candidates.title: The Effect of Digital Storytelling on the Anxiety of Patients with Pituitary Adenoma Undergoing Transsphenoidal Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial.
candidates.abstract: Patients with pituitary adenoma often experience anxiety due to hormonal changes and the stress associated with transsphenoidal surgery. Digital storytelling, as an innovative multimedia-based training method, has recently been used in patient education. This study investigated the effect of digital storytelling on the anxiety of patients with pituitary adenoma undergoing transsphenoidal surgery. This randomized controlled trial was conducted on 70 patients with pituitary adenoma scheduled for transsphenoidal surgery at a teaching hospital affiliated with Tehran University of Medical Sciences. Participants were randomly assigned to an intervention or a control group. The intervention group received a 15-20-minute digital storytelling program that included experiences shared by patients and nurses regarding preoperative and postoperative care, while the control group received routine hospital education. Anxiety levels were measured a day before surgery, a day after surgery, and three weeks later using Spielberger's State Anxiety Scale. Data were analyzed by SPSS-25 software using descriptive and inferential statistics. The mean score of anxiety in the intervention group decreased by 12.45 (1.24) units a day after the surgery and by 24.82 (1.32) units three weeks after the surgery compared to baseline (p < 0.001). A significantly lower anxiety level was observed in the intervention group at both post-intervention time periods compared to the pre-intervention time (F = 17.05, p < 0.001). Repeated measures Analysis of Variance confirmed a significant interaction between time and group (F = 25.31, p < 0.001). Digital storytelling was effective in reducing anxiety among patients with pituitary adenoma undergoing transsphenoidal surgery and may serve as a valuable educational intervention.
candidates.journal: Iranian journal of nursing and midwifery research

candidates.title: Rethinking the Platinum Standard in SCLC: A Meta-Analysis of Limited- and Extensive-Stage Disease in the Immunotherapy Era.
candidates.abstract: SCLC is an aggressive malignancy for which platinum-based chemotherapy is the cornerstone of treatment. Although immunotherapy has redefined the standard of care, the optimal choice between cisplatin and carboplatin remains debated. This study evaluated the impact of platinum backbone selection on survival outcomes across the SCLC spectrum in the immunotherapy era. A systematic review and meta-analysis were performed on randomized controlled trials evaluating first-line chemoimmunotherapy with platinum-based regimens in SCLC. Outcomes were stratified by disease stage and platinum backbone (carboplatin versus cisplatin). Survival end points included progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS). Seven trials (3059 patients) were analyzed. In extensive-stage SCLC (n = 1843), both backbones provided comparable benefits when combined with immunotherapy; the pooled OS hazard ratio (HR) for cisplatin was 0.71 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.57-0.89; p = 0.003) and 0.76 for carboplatin (95% CI: 0.68-0.85; p < 0.001). In limited-stage SCLC (n = 1216), the addition of immunotherapy improved OS (HR: 0.71; 95% CI: 0.54-0.92; p = 0.01) and PFS (HR: 0.70; 95% CI: 0.56-0.87; p = 0.002) in carboplatin-treated patients, whereas, in cisplatin-treated patients the benefit did not reach statistical significance for OS (HR: 1.15; 95% CI: 0.77-1.72; p = 0.49) or PFS (HR: 1.02; 95% CI: 0.81-1.28; p = 0.87). These findings invite a reconsideration of the platinum hierarchy in SCLC management. By demonstrating that carboplatin provides a more effective backbone in the limited-stage setting and comparable efficacy in the extensive-stage setting, this analysis suggests that the historical prioritization of cisplatin may no longer be justified in the era of immunotherapy. Prioritizing carboplatin as a preferred agent may optimize tolerability while preserving or improving survival outcomes across the SCLC spectrum.

candidates.title: Adjuvant radiotherapy in FIGO stage III dMMR endometrial cancer: evidence and perspectives in the molecular era.
candidates.abstract: Current guidelines incorporate chemo-immunotherapy for stage III-IV mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) endometrial cancer, but the evidence supporting omission of adjuvant radiotherapy remains insufficient. Given the pivotal role of pelvic radiotherapy in achieving durable locoregional control in high-risk endometrial cancer, and the lack of robust randomized evidence demonstrating equivalence of systemic therapy alone, the suggestion that EBRT may be safely omitted in the adjuvant treatment of dMMR high-risk disease warrants careful consideration. Importantly, PORTEC-3 (NCT00411138) included radiotherapy in both treatment groups and no immunotherapy, whereas in KEYNOTE-B21 (ENGOT-en11/GOG-3053, NCT04634877) radiotherapy was not randomized; neither trial therefore directly tested the safety of radiotherapy omission. In this Viewpoint, we review current evidence and unresolved questions in the adjuvant management of FIGO stage III dMMR endometrial cancer, with particular attention to the role of radiotherapy in the evolving chemo-immunotherapy era. While our discussion is intentionally focused on dMMR disease, many of the broader considerations regarding the interpretation of emerging evidence and the preservation of effective locoregional treatment are not exclusive to this molecular subgroup. Ongoing trials, including NRG-GY020 (NCT04214067) and the RAINBO MMRd-GREEN trial (ENGOT-en14/GREEN, NCT05255653), are expected to define the optimal integration of immunotherapy and adjuvant radiotherapy in molecularly stratified populations. Beyond survival, locoregional control, recurrence burden, and quality of life remain clinically meaningful endpoints. Future randomized trials should evaluate radiotherapy as an independent treatment variable within molecularly stratified populations, incorporating not only survival but also patterns of failure and patient-reported outcomes. Until such data become available, treatment de-escalation strategies should be adopted with caution.

candidates.title: Complex cardiac overlap: immune checkpoint inhibitor myocarditis in hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy with subsequent NSTEMI.
candidates.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-associated myocarditis is a rare but life-threatening complication, particularly challenging to diagnose in patients with coexisting cardiac conditions. A 58-year-old man with advanced oropharyngeal carcinoma treated with pembrolizumab presented with heart failure symptoms and markedly elevated troponin levels. Imaging revealed hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) alongside cardiac magnetic resonance findings consistent with ICI-associated myocarditis. He initially responded to high-dose corticosteroids but relapsed due to non-adherence, requiring re-treatment and addition of mycophenolate mofetil. Following recovery, he developed a significant rise in troponin with new regional wall motion abnormalities. Coronary angiography demonstrated significant coronary artery disease, supporting the diagnosis of acute coronary syndrome in the context of the clinical presentation, biomarker elevation, and imaging findings, managed with percutaneous coronary intervention. Post-procedural hypotension was attributed to adrenal insufficiency and resolved with stress-dose corticosteroids. Follow-up imaging demonstrated features of both prior myocarditis and new ischemic injury. The patient improved clinically after PCI and was discharged with normalized troponin levels. This case highlights the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges of ICI-associated myocarditis in the presence of overlapping cardiac pathologies. Multimodality imaging and clinical context are essential for accurate diagnosis, and alternative causes of troponin elevation must be carefully excluded.

candidates.title: Medullary thyroid carcinoma with pheochromocytoma and cystic parathyroid degeneration in a ret-negative patient: a case report.
candidates.abstract: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2A (MEN2A) is a rare autosomal dominant hereditary cancer syndrome, predominantly caused by mutations of the RET proto-oncogene on chromosome 10q11.2. It typically presents with medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC), pheochromocytoma, and primary hyperparathyroidism. Cases with a MEN2A phenotype but negative RET testing are uncommon, posing challenges for diagnosis and patient management. We report the case of a 63-year-old female who was diagnosed with MTC and pheochromocytoma. and cystic parathyroid gland. Genetic workup was negative for RET proto-oncogene mutations but positive for a heterozygous variant in the TMEM127 tumor suppressor gene. MEN2A is associated with pathogenic germline variants in the RET proto-oncogene in approximately 95-99% of cases. Our patient, however, exhibited a MEN2A-like clinical phenotype in the absence of an identifiable RET mutation, with a pathogenic TMEM127 variant instead. Although TMEM127 is an established susceptibility gene for pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma, its association with the broader MEN2A phenotype remains unclear. This unusual genotype-phenotype discordance raises important questions regarding the potential role of alternative genetic pathways in MEN2-like syndromes and creates uncertainty regarding postoperative surveillance and the appropriate extent of screening and genetic counseling for family members. Our case represents an unusual scenario where the patient presents with a clinical phenotype of MEN2A but is RET negative and positive heterozygous for a variant in the TMEM127. This atypical genetic finding introduces complexities in determining the appropriate follow-up protocol and the scope of familial screening necessary.

candidates.title: Pediatric sellar and parasellar lesions: a population-based cohort study of presentation, management, and endocrine outcomes.
candidates.abstract: Population-based studies describing the full clinical spectrum of pediatric sellar and parasellar lesions are scarce. Most available data derive from referral-based surgical or diagnosis-specific cohorts. We aimed to characterize presentation, lesion pathology, management, and long-term endocrine outcomes in a population-based cohort. We conducted a retrospective, population-based cohort study of patients aged 18 years or younger diagnosed with sellar or parasellar lesions between 1976 and 2021 in a multicounty region. Clinical presentation, lesion characteristics, management, and endocrine outcomes were abstracted from medical records. Associations were evaluated by lesion type, lesion size (< 10 mm vs. ≥10 mm), and management approach. Among 104 patients, endocrine abnormalities at diagnosis differed by lesion type (p = 0.0004) and were most frequent among patients with pituitary adenomas. Endocrine dysfunction at presentation was more common with lesions ≥ 10 mm than with lesions < 10 mm (74.2% vs. 49.2%; p = 0.0217). Post-treatment endocrine abnormalities were also more common with lesions ≥ 10 mm (64.5% vs. 13.1%; p < 0.0001). Associations with treatment modality were descriptive and subject to confounding by indication. This population-based cohort captured a broad spectrum of pediatric sellar and parasellar disease, including uncommon lesions and conservatively managed cases. Endocrine morbidity was associated with lesion type and size, but clinically relevant abnormalities also occurred in smaller lesions, supporting endocrine evaluation based on clinical context and longitudinal surveillance.

candidates.title: Brief Report: Reassessment of bTMB as a Predictive Biomarker in NSCLC Immunotherapy-A Reanalysis of OAK and POPLAR.
candidates.abstract: Blood-based tumor mutational burden (bTMB) has been proposed as a potential biomarker for identifying patients with advanced NSCLC who may benefit from immunotherapy. Prior studies have primarily focused on the high-bTMB group, which may lead to an incomplete or misleading assessment of the predictive value of bTMB. In this study, we used data from the POPLAR (NCT01903993) and OAK (NCT02008227) trials to re-evaluate the predictive role of bTMB for immunotherapy response in advanced NSCLC by analyzing all patients with available bTMB measures and evaluating outcomes in both high- and low-bTMB groups. Patients with evaluable bTMB from the POPLAR and OAK trials were included. For each study, hazard ratios (HRs) for both progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were calculated separately for the high- and low-bTMB groups across a range of cut points. A total of 211 and 583 patients with evaluable bTMB were included from the POPLAR and OAK trials, respectively. bTMB cut points from 4 to 26 (in increments of 2) were evaluated. At a cut point of 14, one of the evaluated thresholds, in POPLAR, patients with high bTMB had a PFS HR of 0.50 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.30-0.83) and an OS HR of 0.51 (95% CI: 0.30-0.86), whereas patients with low bTMB had a PFS HR of 1.23 (95% CI: 0.86-1.76) and an OS HR of 0.82 (95% CI: 0.55-1.21). In OAK, patients with high-bTMB had a PFS HR of 0.68 (95% CI: 0.50-0.91), and those with low bTMB had a PFS HR of 0.98 (95% CI: 0.79-1.12), with no difference between the two groups for OS (HR = 0.63, 95% CI: 0.45-0.88 versus HR = 0.63, 95% CI: 0.50-0.80). The predictiveness of bTMB in identifying patients with NSCLC who may benefit from immunotherapy was evident for PFS but not for OS. Observing a differential treatment efficacy trend solely within the high-bTMB group across multiple cut points was insufficient to establish predictive utility. A valid assessment requires a comprehensive evaluation of both high- and low-bTMB populations, with predictiveness established by reporting differential treatment efficacy between these two groups.

candidates.title: Shingles With an Unusual Dermatomal Distribution.
candidates.abstract: Shingles, also known as herpes zoster, is a globally recognised, self-limiting infection caused by the reactivation of the varicella-zoster virus (VZV). This virus causes varicella, otherwise known as chickenpox, which is a well-known acute infection, commonly seen among children. Herpes zoster involves an individual nerve and the corresponding dermatome. This case report is written with the intent of reminding clinicians of the variety of ways in which herpes zoster can present. It is important to consider herpes zoster in the differential diagnosis of a rash, even when it is confined to a less common dermatome.

candidates.title: Endoscopic transsphenoidal surgery for a somatotroph pituitary neuroendocrine tumor associated with an infraoptic course of the anterior cerebral artery: A case report.
candidates.abstract: Identifying cerebrovascular anomalies before neurosurgical procedures is essential to avoid intraoperative complications. An infraoptic course of the anterior cerebral artery (IOA) is a rare variant in which the anterior cerebral artery (ACA) arises near the ophthalmic artery and passes beneath the optic nerve. Despite numerous reports of cerebral aneurysms coexisting with IOA, reports of coexistence with brain tumors are extremely rare, and no studies have reported endoscopic transsphenoidal surgery (eTSS) performed for pituitary tumors. Failure to recognize this IOA anomaly preoperatively is critical owing to the risk of vascular injury. A 47-year-old man presented with acromegaly caused by a somatotroph pituitary neuroendocrine tumor. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed a sellar-suprasellar mass, and biochemical testing confirmed excess growth hormone production. After lanreotide-induced tumor shrinkage, surgical treatment was planned. Preoperative MRI, computed tomography angiography, and three-dimensional (3D) fusion imaging demonstrated bilateral IOA and duplication of the left A1 segment. These images enabled a detailed assessment of the tumor, pituitary gland, and vascular anatomy, suggesting that extracapsular resection via eTSS can be safely performed. Intraoperatively, the IOA adhered to the dura as predicted. Total tumor resection was achieved without vascular injury. Postoperative MRI confirmed complete removal, and hormone levels were normalized. IOA is an exceptionally rare vascular anomaly, and unrecognized cases may lead to severe intraoperative complications. This case highlights the importance of meticulous preoperative imaging, particularly 3D fusion techniques, for IOA identification and safe eTSS planning for functional pituitary tumors.

candidates.title: Hyperphagia in Prader-Willi syndrome: linking hypothalamic dysfunction to clinical assessment and management across the lifespan.
candidates.abstract: Prader-Willi syndrome (PWS) is a rare genetic neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by hypothalamic dysfunction and profound dysregulation in hunger and appetite regulation, endocrine function, metabolism and behaviour. Hyperphagia is a defining clinical feature and a major contributor to morbidity, mortality and caregiver burden. Increasing evidence suggests that hyperphagia in PWS represents a multidimensional disorder rather than excessive appetite alone. In December 2024, an international meeting of clinical and scientific experts was convened in Toulouse, France, to explore current understanding of hyperphagia in PWS, challenges in assessment, and evolving approaches to management across the lifespan. Although not a formal consensus process, several consistent themes emerged. These included limitations of existing assessment tools, the need for multidimensional evaluation (including use of instruments such as the Hyperphagia Questionnaire and Hyperphagia Questionnaire for Clinical Trials (HQ-CT). The central role of structured food environments, and vulnerabilities during transition to adult care were also identified as key themes. Experts emphasised that hyperphagia reflects interactions between impaired satiety signalling, activation in reward neurocircuitry, autonomic dysfunction and environmental factors. Management therefore requires integrated biological, behavioural and environmental approaches. While food security and structured support remain foundational, emerging pharmacological therapies may complement multidisciplinary care and reduce caregiver burden. Hyperphagia in PWS should be conceptualised as a complex, multidimensional disorder requiring comprehensive assessment and integrated management. Future priorities include development of additional validated outcome measures, identification of biomarkers, and care models that better align mechanistic insights with real-world clinical practice.
